newsitem.title: PERU: Peru outlines foreign debt payment timetable.
newsitem.headline: Peru outlines foreign debt payment timetable.

text.p: The Peruvian government will make $1.381 billion in foreign debt payments in 1997 after a recent restructuring of debts with commercial banks, Economy Minister Jorge Camet said Thursday.
Of the total, the government has already paid $191 million, Camet told legislators during a congressional hearing.
Camet also outlined the following foreign debt payment timetable from 1998 to 2016:
Peru's total outstanding foreign debt stood at $19.415 billion on March 17, Camet said. Peru has reduced its foreign debt obligations by about one percent a year during the past seven years, he said.
"Peru has the capacity and the possibility to honor its (debt) service," without raising taxes or crimping economic growth, he added.

Outside of its debt restructuring program, the government had not carried out any foreign debt buybacks, Camet said. He said the state bank Banco de la Nacion "as an autonomous entity, has carried out a program of investment in foreign public debt bonds which we will inform about shortly."
